title: Cloudflare global outage from a WAF regex with catastrophic backtracking
symptoms: CPU pinned at 100% across the edge
root_cause: A newly deployed WAF managed rule contained a regular expression with catastrophic backtracking. It ran on every request and drove CPU to 100% globally. A prior refactor had removed the safeguard that limited regex CPU cost, and because it was a security update it skipped the usual gradual rollout.
fix: Global kill switch disabled the WAF to recover CPU, then the offending rule was reverted. Follow-ups: re-add CPU limits on regex evaluation, and route emergency security rules through staged rollout with monitoring.

title: Cloudflare outage from a backbone configuration change misrouting traffic
root_cause: A configuration change intended for a single Atlanta router leaked more broadly and caused all traffic across the backbone to be sent to Atlanta, overwhelming that path and collapsing connectivity for much of the US and Europe.
fix: Rolled back the backbone configuration and drained/rebalanced traffic. Added stronger config validation and blast-radius limits for backbone changes.

title: Cloudflare outage from a BGP prefix ordering change disabling 19 data centers
root_cause: A change to the ordering of BGP prefix advertisements during a network topology migration caused the busiest 19 data centers to stop announcing routes, taking them offline.
fix: Reverted the network configuration to restore prefix advertisements. Introduced better staged rollout and review for BGP/topology changes.

title: Cloudflare control-plane outage from a service token management code error
root_cause: A code change in service token management contained an error that disabled parts of the control plane (Workers, Zero Trust, CDN configuration APIs) for about two hours.
fix: Rolled back the change and restored the control plane. Added tests and safeguards around token management code paths.

title: Cloudflare control plane and analytics outage from a data center power failure
root_cause: A power failure at a third-party (Flexential) data center hosting core control-plane services, combined with insufficient redundancy and dependencies that did not fail over cleanly, took down the control plane and analytics while the edge kept serving traffic.
fix: Restored power and services, then re-architected for higher availability across data centers and reduced hidden single-facility dependencies.

title: Fastly global CDN outage from a latent software bug triggered by a config change
root_cause: A software deployment weeks earlier introduced a latent bug that could be triggered under specific conditions. A valid customer configuration change later triggered it, causing most edge nodes to return errors globally.
fix: Identified and disabled the triggering configuration, then patched the underlying bug. Improved detection and rollout safeguards for such latent conditions.

title: AWS S3 us-east-1 outage from a mistyped command removing too much capacity
root_cause: During routine debugging an engineer ran a command with a typo that removed far more S3 subsystem capacity than intended, forcing a full restart of index and placement subsystems that took hours and impaired many dependent services.
fix: Restarted the affected subsystems and restored capacity. Added guardrails to the tooling to prevent removing capacity below safe minimums and to slow large capacity changes.

title: AWS Kinesis us-east-1 outage from exceeding an operating-system thread limit
symptoms: elevated Kinesis API errors and latency
root_cause: A small capacity addition pushed the number of threads in the Kinesis front-end fleet past the operating-system thread limit per server. Front-end servers began failing, and because many AWS services depend on Kinesis the impact cascaded widely.
fix: Rolled back the capacity addition and restarted the front-end fleet, then increased thread limits and re-architected the front-end to reduce per-server thread counts.

title: AWS EBS/EC2 us-east-1 outage from a re-mirroring storm after a network change
root_cause: A network configuration change during scaling routed EBS traffic onto a lower-capacity network. When the primary network was restored, a large set of volumes simultaneously tried to re-mirror, exhausting spare capacity and creating a self-reinforcing storm that overwhelmed the control plane.
fix: Throttled and manually recovered re-mirroring, added capacity, and prevented control-plane overload. Improved network change procedures and back-off in the re-mirroring logic.

title: AWS EC2 DNS resolver outage from a config change removing minimum healthy hosts
symptoms: EC2 DNS query failures for ~84 minutes
root_cause: A configuration change removed the setting that maintained a minimum number of healthy hosts for the DNS resolver fleet, allowing the fleet to shrink below what was needed to serve queries.
fix: Restored the minimum healthy hosts configuration and the fleet. Added validation so changes cannot drop the fleet below a safe minimum.

title: Facebook/Meta global outage from a backbone BGP withdrawal breaking DNS
root_cause: A command issued during routine backbone maintenance was intended to assess capacity but unintentionally took down all backbone connections. An audit tool that should have blocked it had a bug. With the backbone down, the DNS servers withdrew their BGP routes, making the entire platform unresolvable.
fix: Engineers restored the backbone on-site (access itself was hampered by the outage). Added safeguards to the maintenance tooling and improved out-of-band recovery access.

title: Google Compute Engine global connectivity loss from withdrawn IP block advertisements
symptoms: global loss of GCE connectivity for ~18 minutes
root_cause: An autogenerated network configuration removed all Google Compute Engine IP blocks from BGP announcements, cutting external connectivity. A race and insufficient canarying in the config pipeline allowed the bad config to roll out.
fix: Reverted to the previous network configuration to restore announcements. Hardened the config generation pipeline with canarying and progressive rollout.

title: Google services global outage from an autogenerated configuration error
symptoms: multiple Google services unavailable briefly worldwide
root_cause: An internal system generated an invalid configuration that was sent to live services, causing them to malfunction until the configuration was corrected.
fix: Pushed a corrected configuration and added validation on generated configs before distribution.

title: Datadog multi-region outage from an auto-update wiping network rules
root_cause: A security update to systemd on the fleet automatically restarted systemd-networkd, which removed the network rules Cilium relies on. This severed connectivity for Cilium-protected Kubernetes nodes across multiple regions simultaneously.
fix: Restored networking on affected nodes and paused the auto-update. Pinned/controlled the systemd update and decoupled it from the network policy layer.

title: GitHub 24-hour degradation from a 43-second network partition and MySQL failover
root_cause: Routine replacement of failing optical equipment briefly (43s) partitioned the US East Coast data center. In that window the primary accepted writes that were not replicated west; Orchestrator then failed clusters over to the West Coast, leaving databases divergent and requiring careful reconciliation.
fix: Reconciled divergent writes and restored consistency. Adjusted Orchestrator/failover behavior to be more conservative about topology changes triggered by short partitions.

title: GitLab.com database outage and data loss from deleting the wrong directory
root_cause: While troubleshooting replication lag caused by a load spike, an engineer intending to clear a secondary's data directory ran the deletion against the primary. Multiple backup and replication mechanisms were then discovered to be broken, so several hours of data could not be recovered.
fix: Restored from a several-hours-old snapshot. Overhauled backups, added verification, and improved runbooks and safeguards for destructive operations.

title: GitHub 36-minute outage from a database config change failing health checks
root_cause: A database configuration change broke the routing service's health checks, causing a production read endpoint to be marked unhealthy and traffic to be pulled away, resulting in broad failures.
fix: Reverted the configuration change and restored routing. Improved testing of health-check-affecting configuration changes.

title: Stripe 90-minute API outage from an incorrectly executed database migration
root_cause: A manual database operation was run without a required dependency in place, which took a critical index offline and caused API requests depending on it to fail.
fix: Restored the index and completed the migration correctly. Added checks and safer procedures for manual database operations.

title: CircleCI jobs stuck from a PostgreSQL field-type change conflicting with old rows
root_cause: A deploy changed a PostgreSQL field's type. Newly written rows used the new type while older rows used the old type, and the mismatch broke job distribution until data was reconciled.
fix: Reconciled the conflicting rows and corrected the schema/deploy. Adopted safer, backward-compatible migration patterns.

title: Slack outage from a cache node removal overloading the Vitess database tier
root_cause: Removing a cache node shifted load onto the Vitess database cluster. The sudden increase in cache misses overloaded the database tier, causing high latency and errors.
fix: Restored cache capacity and shed load until the database recovered. Improved cache-node change procedures and database headroom.

title: Slack outage from AWS Transit Gateway saturation and packet loss during scale-up
root_cause: A traffic surge after the holidays saturated AWS Transit Gateways, which had not scaled up automatically fast enough, causing packet loss. Autoscaling attempts under load initially made things worse by adding to the strain.
fix: Manually scaled the Transit Gateways and provisioning to relieve saturation. Pre-scaled capacity and improved autoscaling responsiveness for network components.

title: Slack outage from cascading connection failures exceeding database capacity
symptoms: up to 2 hours for ~5% of users
root_cause: A combination of factors disconnected a large number of users at once. Their simultaneous reconnects exceeded database capacity, and the resulting connection storm cascaded into broader failures.
fix: Shed load and staggered reconnects to let the database recover. Added backpressure and capacity to handle reconnect storms.

title: Roblox 73-hour outage from Consul streaming and BoltDB write contention
root_cause: Enabling a new Consul streaming feature under high load interacted badly with BoltDB write performance, causing severe contention and leader-election instability across the Consul cluster that Roblox's services depend on for discovery and configuration.
fix: Disabled the streaming feature, rebuilt Consul on faster storage, and reduced write pressure. Worked with HashiCorp on the underlying issues.

title: Windows Azure global outage from a leap-year certificate date calculation bug
root_cause: Transient certificates were generated with a validity end date of the current date plus one year. On Feb 29, 2012 this produced Feb 29, 2013, an invalid date, so certificate creation failed. That broke the guest-agent to host handshake and cascaded through the fabric controller as it marked hardware faulty.
fix: Corrected the date calculation and recovered the fabric. Added handling for date-arithmetic edge cases and limited cascading fault behavior.

title: Firefox add-ons disabled worldwide by an expired intermediate certificate
root_cause: The intermediate certificate used to sign browser add-ons expired, so Firefox treated all add-ons as invalid and disabled them.
fix: Shipped a new valid certificate via a system add-on / Studies mechanism to re-enable add-ons, then patched the signing lifecycle. Added monitoring for certificate expiry.

title: Firefox global hang from an HTTP/3 code path in the network stack
root_cause: A change in how a load balancer sent HTTP/3 responses triggered a bug in Firefox's network stack that caused an infinite loop / hang, making the browser unresponsive for many users.
fix: Mitigated by changing the server-side HTTP/3 behavior, then patched the client network stack. Added tests for the failing condition.

title: CrowdStrike Falcon content update crashing Windows hosts worldwide
root_cause: A rapid-release content update contained a fault that the deployment validator failed to catch. The sensor's kernel driver performed an out-of-bounds memory read on the malformed content, crashing Windows into boot loops.
fix: Reverted the content within ~78 minutes and shipped remediation guidance. Added validation, staged/canary rollout for content updates, and customer-side rollout controls.

title: Knight Capital $460M loss from an incomplete deploy reactivating dead code
root_cause: A deploy to eight servers was applied to only seven. A reused feature flag reactivated old, long-dead code ("Power Peg") on the un-updated server, which sent a flood of unintended orders to the market.
fix: Halted trading and unwound positions (too late to avoid the loss). Lessons: automated, verified deploys to all hosts; never reuse flags; kill switches and pre-trade risk limits.

title: Atlassian multi-week outage from a maintenance script deleting customer sites
root_cause: A maintenance script meant to remove a legacy app used the wrong identifiers and permanently deleted entire customer sites instead. Restores had to be done largely one customer at a time, extending recovery for weeks.
fix: Built and parallelized a bulk restore process to recover sites. Added safeguards (soft-delete, dry-run, review) for destructive bulk operations and a faster large-scale restore capability.

title: Reddit Pi-Day outage from a Kubernetes upgrade breaking node routing
root_cause: A Kubernetes version upgrade changed how a node label was used, which broke Calico's route reflector configuration and node-to-node routing, taking the cluster (and thus the site) down.
fix: Rolled back the cluster and restored routing. Improved upgrade testing, especially for network/label-dependent components, and recovery runbooks.

title: Reddit outage from an error during a backend system migration
root_cause: An error during a critical backend migration (disabling a component while performing maintenance) disrupted the system that manages processing capacity, causing an outage and degradation.
fix: Reverted the change and restored the affected system. Added safeguards and clearer runbooks for the migration.

title: GitHub outage from a brief power disruption at the primary data center
root_cause: A brief disruption to the electrical systems at the primary data center caused a significant portion of servers to reboot at once, taking down services until they recovered.
fix: Recovered services after power was restored and improved resilience to power events, including failover practices.

title: ChatGPT outage and data exposure from a Redis client cache bug
symptoms: some users saw others' chat titles and limited billing info
root_cause: A change increased load and, combined with a bug in the Redis client library, caused canceled requests to corrupt connections so that some cached responses were returned for the wrong user, exposing limited data.
fix: Took ChatGPT offline, patched the Redis client usage, and added checks. Notified affected users and reviewed caching for correctness under cancellation.

title: Cloudflare outage from an oversized bot-detection feature file after a DB permissions change
root_cause: A database permissions change caused a query to return duplicate rows, doubling the size of the bot-detection feature file. The oversized file exceeded a hard limit in the proxy, causing the bot module to fail and edge requests to error systemwide.
fix: Reverted to a known-good feature file and restored the query behavior, then added size validation and safer handling when the feature file is malformed.

title: Okta security incident from a compromised third-party support engineer laptop
root_cause: An attacker gained control of a support engineer's laptop at a third-party subprocessor, giving limited access to Okta support tooling and a small number of customers.
fix: Revoked access, investigated scope, and tightened subprocessor security controls and monitoring.

title: Parity multi-sig wallet hack from an under-reviewed contract change
root_cause: A large change containing a security-critical bug was mislabeled as a UI change and inadequately reviewed. The vulnerability let an attacker take ownership of multi-sig wallets and drain funds.
fix: Patched the contract and (via white-hat action) rescued at-risk funds. Emphasized security review for all changes regardless of labeling.

title: CircleCI UI/build issues from an out-of-band WAF change enabled by an IAM gap
root_cause: An IAM role gap allowed a WAF change to be made outside the Terraform pipeline. Because the change was not recorded as part of normal change management, it slowed detection when it started blocking legitimate traffic.
fix: Reverted the WAF change and closed the IAM gap so all WAF changes flow through the pipeline with an audit trail.

title: Cloudflare outage from a router configuration change during an attack mitigation
root_cause: A rule intended to mitigate an attack was pushed to the edge routers but triggered a bug that caused the routers to stop forwarding traffic, taking the network offline.
fix: Removed the rule and rebooted routers to recover. Improved validation and rollout for edge network rules.
